## What actually ran

You used **Manual Deploy** with a `deploy_ref` (tag `v1.3.2+warranty+zibra+cruize` or SHA `05e8bb7`). Any non-empty `deploy_ref` sets `PINNED=true` and takes the **commit-pinned rollback** path.

That is not the â€œprod tag labels the runâ€ path. That other path only runs when `deploy_ref` is **empty** and the workflow itself is started from a tag. Your log shows `PINNED: true` and `Ref type: branch` (workflow started from `main`).

## Why it blocked

Pinned Zibra prod starts CodePipeline at that commit. The pipelineâ€™s **UpdatePipeline** stage then applies `sam/pipeline/prod/zibra-codepipeline.yaml` **from the pinned commit**. `RestartExecutionOnUpdate: true` is on.

After `05e8bb7`, main gained:

`0fb47bb` â€” **FIX | Zibra Build-integrity Gap (#405)**

```diff
- BuildSpec: sam/pipeline/buildspec_deploy.yml
+ BuildSpec: sam/pipeline/buildspec_zibra_deploy.yml
```

That is the `1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)` in the log.

If the pin were allowed, UpdatePipeline would put the **old shared buildspec** back, then restart at `origin/main` HEAD. You would lose the integrity-gap buildspec and could redeploy current main instead of the tag.

The guard in `manual-deploy.yml` exists for exactly this. README already documents it: do not pin a commit that predates the last change to that projectâ€™s pipeline YAML.

## How to deploy

**Current prod Zibra (including #405):** leave `deploy_ref` empty. Environment `prod`, project `Zibra`, run the workflow from `main`. That starts the live pipeline at current `main`.

**A later commit that already has `buildspec_zibra_deploy.yml`:** you can pin that SHA/tag. Anything **at or after** `0fb47bb` / `0d7022f` (`Release | Build-integrity gap`) matches `origin/main`â€™s pipeline YAML.

**Tag `v1.3.2+warranty+zibra+cruize` (`05e8bb7`):** you cannot pin it safely. That release is older than the pipeline YAML change. Rolling the app back to that tag would also roll the pipeline back to `buildspec_deploy.yml`.

If you intended â€œdeploy current main and just label it with the tag,â€ use an empty `deploy_ref`. If you intended a real rollback to `v1.3.2`, say so â€” that needs a different process than this workflowâ€™s pin path. I will not start a prod pipeline from this session.

[PR #413](https://github.com/CarbizRentals/carbiz-aws-iac/pull/413) is a **merged release from `uat` into `main`**: **â€œRelease | Build-integrity gap (Zibra Security)â€**.

It ships two things.

**1. The main Zibra fix**  
Stops `500`s on Zibra `/v1/get` and `/v1/fetch/file`, and closes a **dist build-integrity gap** (the packaged Lambda `dist/` did not reliably match source). That includes:

- Safer SOQL building (encoding, escaping, query conversion)
- Clearer client vs server query errors
- A dedicated Zibra deploy buildspec and dist packaging (`write-dist-package.js`, committed `dist` lockfile)
- A large new Zibra test suite

**2. Other UAT work that rode along**  
Because this is `uat` â†’ `main`, it also includes earlier UAT merges:

- Align toll processor/batcher repo code with what production already runs
- Point UAT toll pipelines at the `uat` branch (`TargetBranch` / `FeatureGitBranch` defaults)

Author is Dedi Hermanto. Notion write-up: [Fix Zibra /v1/get + /v1/fetch/file 500 and close dist build-integrity gap](https://app.notion.com/p/carbiz/Fix-Zibra-v1-get-v1-fetch-file-500-and-close-dist-build-integrity-gap-390e109ba14e81259259c0050a9fdae0).

1. Source checks out the **pinned** commit.
2. `UpdatePipeline` applies **that commitâ€™s** `zibra-codepipeline.yaml`.
3. `RestartExecutionOnUpdate: true` is set on the pipeline.

If the old YAML is applied, CodePipeline treats that as a definition change and starts a **new** execution at **`origin/main` HEAD**. That would redeploy current main â€” the build you are trying to roll away from â€” instead of `05e8bb7`.

How it is supposed to work:
1. `deploy_ref=<tag>` resolves to a commit on the env branch and starts CodePipeline with `--source-revisions`.
2. If `zibra-codepipeline.yaml` matches the branch, start with `SkipSelfMutation=true` so `UpdatePipeline` is skipped.
3. If it differs, pre-sync the live pipeline stack from the tag, fence `RestartExecutionOnUpdate` by blocking inbound to `UpdatePipeline`, abandon the auto-started HEAD run, then start the pinned execution.

The `VariableCheck` / `Result: SKIP` logic is correct: skip when `SkipSelfMutation` is not `"false"`. The fencing idea (disable transition *before* the stack update) is also the right shape. The gap is what happens after pre-sync.

On current `main`, **Manual Deploy does not deploy Lambdas itself**. It assumes a GitHub OIDC role and starts (or retargets) the projectâ€™s long-lived **CodePipeline**. CodePipeline then sources git, may self-update, waits for prod approval, and runs CodeBuild/`sam deploy`.

Merging to `main` does not start prod pipelines (`DetectChanges: false`). This workflow is the start button.

## What you select

The workflow is `workflow_dispatch` only. You choose:

| Input | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Use workflow from** | Which git ref GitHub checks out, and which workflow YAML runs. This also becomes `$BRANCH`. |
| **environment** | Which AWS account: prod `7673â€¦`, UAT `7170â€¦`, dev `0582â€¦`. |
| **project** | Which pipeline stack/name to start. |
| **deploy_ref** | Optional tag or SHA. Empty = â€œdeploy the pipelineâ€™s current branch HEADâ€. |

```34:38:.github/workflows/manual-deploy.yml
      deploy_ref:
        description: 'Tag or commit SHA for rollback (optional â€” leave empty for normal branch deploy)'
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
```

## Run sequence

1. Check out the selected ref (`fetch-depth: 0`).
2. Resolve `deploy_ref` (if set) to a 40-character commit, including annotated tags via `^{commit}`.
3. Map environment â†’ account role; map project + environment â†’ pipeline stack name and pipeline name. Some projects (Salesforce, public API) resolve the physical pipeline name from the stack.
4. Assume `GitHubActionsRole` via OIDC.
5. Take one of three deploy paths.

V2 `--source-revisions` (the only way to pin a commit) is allowed only for:

- all envs: `loan-cars`, `cruize-control`, `publicAPI`, `Zibra`
- **non-prod only**: `dealershipAPI`, `toll-processor`, `tollBatcher`

Prod `salesforce`, `dealershipAPI`, `tollBatcher`, `toll-processor`, Cognito, bonus-referral are not V2 and cannot take a pin.

## The three paths

### 1. `deploy_ref` set â€” pin a tag/SHA

This is the rollback path.

```
resolve SHA â†’ must be an ancestor of the env branch
  prod â†’ origin/main
  uat  â†’ origin/uat
  dev  â†’ origin/develop
â†’ project must be V2
â†’ pinned commitâ€™s pipeline YAML must be byte-identical to the env branchâ€™s YAML
â†’ start CodePipeline with --source-revisions COMMIT_ID=<sha>
```

If the tagâ€™s `sam/pipeline/<env>/<project>-codepipeline.yaml` differs from the environment branch, the job **exits**. It does not pre-sync the stack. That guard exists because `UpdatePipeline` plus `RestartExecutionOnUpdate: true` would apply the old pipeline definition, then start a **new** execution at branch HEAD and redeploy what you were rolling away from.

So on current `main`, a specified tag deploys **only if** that tag is already on the env branch **and** it does not change that projectâ€™s pipeline YAML (for Zibra, that includes the CodeBuild `BuildSpec` path).

### 2. Prod + â€œUse workflow fromâ€ is a tag + empty `deploy_ref`

```441:446:.github/workflows/manual-deploy.yml
        elif [ "$ENVIRONMENT" = "prod" ] && [ "$REF_TYPE" = "tag" ]; then
          echo "Prod tag ref - triggering pipeline directly (stack tracks main; tag labels the run)"
          echo "Starting pipeline execution for $PROJECT..."
          aws codepipeline start-pipeline-execution --name $PIPELINE_NAME
```

This does **not** pin the tag. It starts the pipeline with no source revision. The pipeline still sources **`main` HEAD**. The tag only names the Actions run. This is the common footgun if someone tries to â€œdeploy a tagâ€ from the branch dropdown.

### 3. Branch deploy (empty `deploy_ref`)

Allowed refs: `main`, `develop`, `uat`, `release/*`, `hotfix/*`, `feat/*`, `fix/*`.

It reads the stackâ€™s `FeatureGitBranch`:

- **Same as the workflow branch** (or the stack has no such parameter and you ran from `main`): if the pipeline is already `InProgress`, it skips; otherwise it starts an unpinned execution. Source is whatever `BranchName` the pipeline already has (`main` for prod Zibra).
- **Different branch**: `update-stack --use-previous-template` with the new `FeatureGitBranch`. It does not call `start-pipeline-execution`. The stack update plus `RestartExecutionOnUpdate` is what starts the run. Prod Zibra has no `FeatureGitBranch`; running this path from anything other than `main` fails (â€œdoes not support retargetingâ€).

## What happens after Actions finishes

Actions only starts CodePipeline. A typical Zibra/prod run is:

**Source** (`main`, or the pinned SHA) â†’ **UpdatePipeline** (applies pipeline YAML from that source) â†’ **WaitForManualApproval** (prod only) â†’ **BuildAndDeploy** (CodeBuild + the buildspec on that pipeline).

Dev/UAT skip the approval stage. Prod still needs the CodePipeline approval; this workflow does not bypass it.

## Practical use on current `main`

**Normal prod ship:** Use workflow from `main`, environment `prod`, project e.g. `Zibra`, leave `deploy_ref` empty. Then approve in CodePipeline.

**Rollback to a tag:** Use workflow from `main` (so you run this YAML), environment `prod`, `deploy_ref=<tag>`. The tag must already be on `main`, and that tag must not have a different pipeline YAML than current `main`. Otherwise the job fails on purpose.

**Do not** pick the old tag in â€œUse workflow fromâ€ and leave `deploy_ref` empty. That path deploys current `main`.

It is a **rollback safety check**, not a generic â€œYAML must be tidyâ€ lint.

**What it does**

On a pinned Manual Deploy it diffs the projectâ€™s CodePipeline template:

`pinned commit` vs `origin/main` (prod) â€” for Zibra that file is `sam/pipeline/prod/zibra-codepipeline.yaml`.

If those files differ, the workflow **refuses to start the pipeline**.

**Why it exists**

Prod Zibra is a **self-mutating** pipeline:

1. **Source** checks out the commit you pinned.
2. **UpdatePipeline** applies **that commitâ€™s** `zibra-codepipeline.yaml` to the live stack (`TemplatePath: SourceCodeAsZip::sam/pipeline/prod/zibra-codepipeline.yaml`).
3. The pipeline has `RestartExecutionOnUpdate: true`.

So a pin is not â€œbuild this old Lambda and leave the pipeline alone.â€ The first thing it does is try to **move the live pipeline definition backward**.

If that YAML is older than `main` (your case: old `buildspec_deploy.yml` vs current `buildspec_zibra_deploy.yml`), CloudFormation sees a real definition change. With `RestartExecutionOnUpdate`, AWS then starts a **new** execution. That new run sources **`main` HEAD**, not the pin. You can end up **redeploying the build you were rolling away from**, and you may also **revert the live pipeline** to the old template.

The guard blocks that loop **before** `start-pipeline-execution`.

**Is it necessary?**

**Yes, with the pipeline as it is today.** Without it, a pin across a pipeline-YAML change is unsafe. That is exactly why `05e8bb7` / `v1.3.2+â€¦` was rejected.

It is **not** necessary in the abstract. You could drop it only if you also changed the design, for example:

- turn off `RestartExecutionOnUpdate`, **or**
- skip `UpdatePipeline` on pinned runs, **or**
- stop applying pipeline YAML from the same source artifact as the Lambda.

None of that is true for prod Zibra now.

**What it does *not* mean**

It does not mean you can never roll back. It means: pin a commit whose **pipeline YAML matches current `main`**, and only roll back application/Lambda commits. If the bad Lambda and the YAML change landed together (PR #413), you need a **new `main` commit** that reverts ZibraHandler and **keeps** todayâ€™s pipeline YAML.

Bypassing the guard to pin `v1.3.2` would be the dangerous option, not the necessary one.

Yes. Wanting â€œall the code at that timeâ€ is a reasonable rollback. The guard still makes sense because **this pipeline cannot do that safely**.

A pin does not mean â€œfreeze the world at commit X and deploy it.â€ For prod Zibra it means:

1. Start an execution whose **Source** is commit X.
2. **UpdatePipeline** immediately applies **Xâ€™s** `zibra-codepipeline.yaml` to the **live** pipeline.
3. `RestartExecutionOnUpdate: true` then starts a **new** execution.

That new run does **not** keep your pin. It uses the pipelineâ€™s default source: **`main` HEAD**.

So if Xâ€™s pipeline YAML differs from `main` (your case):

| What you want | What actually happens |
|---|---|
| Build and deploy snapshot X (old Lambda + old YAML) | First run starts rewriting the live pipeline to old YAML |
| Stay on X | Restart kicks a second run at **current `main`** |
| Prod = that old release | Second run can redeploy the release you are rolling away from, and put the pipeline YAML back (or race the two deploys) |

The guard is not saying â€œold YAML is wrong.â€ It is saying â€œa YAML diff on a pin **triggers that restart loop**, so you do not get a snapshot deploy.â€

That is why the README treats pin as **Lambda/app rollback only**, with pipeline YAML left at current `main`. â€œAll code at that timeâ€ would only work if you also changed the mechanism, for example:

- `RestartExecutionOnUpdate: false` on pinned runs, or
- skip `UpdatePipeline` when the source is pinned, or
- a one-off `sam deploy` of the old app stack **without** going through this self-mutating pipeline.

None of those are what Manual Deploy + prod Zibra does today.

**Bottom line:** your rollback goal is fine; this guard matches the current pipeline. Removing it so you can pin `v1.3.2` would not give you â€œall the code at that time.â€ It would give you the restart-at-`main` behaviour the check exists to stop.

To get that old Zibra Lambda out, put a **new commit on `main`** that restores the old app code and **keeps todayâ€™s pipeline YAML**, then deploy that.

**The security model is genuinely well built** in the areas it covers. Two-layer auth (API Gateway JWT authorizer plus an independent in-Lambda Cognito `getUser`), seven named `assert*Owned` helpers that re-read the target through a tenant-scoped query and return a *verified* ID that replaces the caller's, deny-by-default on creates (`UNGATED_CREATE_OBJECT` for any object without an explicit gate), and allowlist-based log redaction. Related: no Stripe idempotency keys anywhere, so a retry can duplicate customers and intents; and the legacy `POST /v1/create/payment-intent` is still deployed alongside its replacement while creating a Stripe customer *before* payment succeeds.

`validateToken` **hardcodes Cognito pool IDs** in an inline ternary on `process.env.ENVIRONMENT`, while the SAM template selects the pool via `FindInMap` on `LambdaEnvironment`. Two mechanisms driven by two different variables in a security-critical component.

The **`Account` schema object has no tenant filter**. It's safe today only because `POST /v1/getUserCompany` forces the object name and rejects a non-empty body â€” but that's an implicit coupling, and `Account` is also the Salesforce object behind `Dealerships`, `Location`, and `Program`, which *do* carry filters.

**The best decision in the codebase, and it's worth copying.** Zibra serves Carbiz's own branch network, so scope is branch-based rather than program/location â€” but crucially, `isMasterView` (the flag that lifts all branch filtering) is **read from the Salesforce User record via Apex, not from a Cognito attribute**. Granting estate-wide visibility requires a change in the system of record, not an edit to a token claim. It fails closed on a missing user row, and a caller with no branches gets a `__NO_BRANCH_ACCESS__` sentinel that matches nothing. Seven purpose-built visibility helpers enforce it, all traversing to `Job__c` since that's the only object carrying a direct branch reference.

The other standout is `repository/` â€” a typed TypeScript layer with branded composite-reference types and `allOrNone: true` on the composite request. Accident intake creates seven Salesforce objects atomically. It's the only place in the three middle-tier Lambdas where a multi-object business transaction genuinely rolls back, which matters here because that data supports insurance claims.

**The finding I'd fix first is `mysql.format()` being used to escape SOQL.** Seven files build Salesforce queries with the MySQL driver's escaper, then strip the backticks it adds:

```javascript
mysql.format(`SELECT+Id+FROM+Job__c+WHERE+Id=?+AND+Branch__r.Name+IN+(${placeholders})+LIMIT+1`,
             [jobId, ...branchNames]).replaceAll('`', '')
```

MySQL and SOQL have different escaping rules â€” the `.replaceAll` is itself evidence of the mismatch. It's safe today because the values are validated Salesforce IDs, but branch *names* also flow through, and those come partly from a Cognito attribute and aren't constrained to a safe character set. Compounding it, the dependency is `"mysql": "github:mysqljs/mysql"` â€” an unpinned git dependency on an unmaintained package, bundled into a Lambda handling accident data. Replacing it with a real SOQL escaper resolves both at once. `buildJobVisibilityQuery` is already exported separately from `isJobVisible`, so it looks like it was written to be testable â€” the tests just don't exist yet.

Two more worth your attention. **Branch identity is a mutable name**, not an ID, so renaming a branch in Salesforce silently revokes access for anyone whose Cognito attribute still holds the old name. And **`services/stripe/paymentIntent.js` is the same 269-line module as Loan Cars'** â€” same three functions, same signatures, two copies. It carries the same gaps (no idempotency keys, the weaker single-shot route is the one in use, no webhook) and here the contrast is sharper: in a codebase with seven helpers dedicated to proving a caller may touch a record, the payment routes resolve no scope and check no ownership at all. I've cross-linked the finding from both sides.

Another marked `[SECURITY]` says the code logs full bearer tokens, with a worked example; the code beneath masks them. And `index.js` has `// AUDIT LOG MISSING [CHANGE]` sitting directly above the audit log it claims is missing. All three describe problems that were fixed without removing the annotation. Worth deleting â€” stale `CRITICAL` markers train reviewers to skim security comments, and the second one contains a copyable example of a logged token.

**The headline for the frontend itself: it enforces nothing, deliberately.** All 14 routes render for any authenticated user â€” no equivalent of the Loan Cars gates on `profileType`, `portalServices`, or `hasPermission`. `hasMasterView` and `userBranches` are fetched only to build the sidebar. That's the correct architecture, since a React bundle is readable and editable by its user, and it pairs with the strongest server-side model in the estate. But it means the entire access-control surface sits in one Lambda whose seven visibility helpers have no tests â€” which remains the most consequential risk across both packages.

**The bug I'd fix first is two lines.** Both uses of `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` render `record.jobURL`, which the API builds as a *plain* URL string from a Secrets Manager value plus a Salesforce ID. Nothing user-controlled reaches it, so it isn't exploitable â€” but injecting a bare URL as `innerHTML` produces unclickable text under a tooltip reading "Open job in Salesforce". The server helper's docstring emphasises "plain", which reads like the note of someone who changed it from returning an anchor tag; the frontend was never updated. Swapping in a real `<a>` fixes the broken column and takes the package's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` count to zero.

Two things this package does **better** than Loan Cars, worth noting since I flagged the opposites there: `aws-exports.js` is gitignored and the README documents it with placeholders rather than a live pool ID; and the rental agreement text is 1,360 lines of static JSX rather than program-supplied HTML through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

Three more findings recorded: **zero automated tests** for ~8,100 lines despite a correct `jest.config.js` and all three Testing Library packages declared â€” `package.json` has no `test` script at all, so `yarn test` does nothing; **`loadStripe` is called inside the component body** so a new promise is created every render, with a `throw` in the render path turning a missing env var into a blank screen; and **the client can't express multi-branch access** â€” it returns `userBranches: [oneBranch]` while the API merges in `custom:ADDITIONAL_BRANCHES`, so a user granted extra branches server-side has no way to reach them.

One thing I hadn't expected: there's a **second, browser-side ProofTec integration**, separate from the server-side AppSync client. The SPA exchanges the user's Cognito ID token for a short-lived opaque handover code via ProofTec's `ssoGraphqlAPI`, so raw JWTs never land in a deeplink URL. Good reasoning, clearly documented in the README â€” the residual questions are that an ID token carrying email and name goes to a third party from the browser, the endpoint is configured per-branch in the Amplify Console (invisible to code review), and a misconfiguration falls back *silently* to the older sign-in path with no error or log.

## How Nintex is used

Nintex DocGen is one of three Salesforce document renderers behind a single internal dispatcher (with S-Docs and FormTitan). Callers publish `DocGen_Request__e`; they do not call Nintex directly.

| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| `DocGen_Request__e` | Internal platform event (not relayed to AWS) |
| `Ddp_Id__c` | **Nintex DocGen document package** (the only field the vault ties specifically to Nintex) |
| `Document_Route__c` | Vendor route (S-Docs / Nintex / FormTitan) |
| `Delivery_Option_Id__c` | Delivery method |
| `Source_Application__c` / `Source_Record_Id__c` | Caller and originating record |
| `Correlation_Id__c` | Trace ID (only correlation ID on any org event) |
| `DocGenRequestTrigger` | Subscriber (API 65, last modified 2026-08-10) |
| `DocGenRequestHandler` | Trigger handler |
| `Central DocGen Dispatcher` | Routes the request to the vendor package |

This is **AD-13** in Architecture Decisions: a central dispatcher so callers stay decoupled from three competing packages.

Nintex also appears as:

- A **connected app** named Nintex DocGen
- Installed-package Lightning apps labelled **Loop** (Nintex DocGen / Drawloop)
- Permission sets `DDP_Administrator` and `DDP_User_All` (replacements for deprecated `DDP_Admin` / `DDP_User`)

These are generation **workflows**. The vault does **not** say they use the Nintex route (`Ddp_Id__c`) rather than S-Docs or FormTitan.

PR [#432](https://github.com/CarbizRentals/carbiz-aws-iac/pull/432) does **not** leave `GET /dealerships` open. It swaps Ed25519 signed-request auth for a **static Bearer token** in Lambda. That is weaker, and the table is **PII**, not a bland Excel dump.

**What changed**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `sam/dealership-api-template.yaml` | `GET /dealerships` â†’ `Authorizer: NONE`; `VALID_TOKEN` from SSM `/dealership/apiauthorizer/validtoken` into the Lambda env |
| `helpers/verifyAuthorization.mjs` | Require `Authorization: Bearer â€¦` and compare to `VALID_TOKEN` with `timingSafeEqual` |
| `index.mjs` | List GET uses Bearer check; POST / GET-by-id / DELETE still use signed-request + body hash |

POST and DELETE stay on `SignedRequestAuthorizerV3`. That part is fine.

The `dealership` items are company names, ABNs, addresses, and staff **names, emails, and mobiles**. Anyone with the token gets a full `Scan` of that table.

---

**Severity:** High  
**Confidence:** Confirmed  
**Category:** Security  
**Location:** `sam/dealership-api-template.yaml` (`DealershipListGet` `Authorizer: NONE`, `VALID_TOKEN` env); `verifyAuthorization.mjs`  
**Finding:** Gateway auth is removed. The only control is a **long-lived shared secret**. CloudFormation writes that secret into the Lambda environment. Anyone with `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` (or a leaked Power Automate connection / run history) can read it and dump the table. Unlike signed requests, there is no timestamp, nonce, or request binding â€” replay works until the token is rotated. CORS is `AllowOrigins: '*'`, so a browser that has the token can call the route too.  
**Impact:** Unauthenticated callers still get 401/403, but a single leaked Bearer value exposes all dealer PII.  
**Recommendation:** Do not store the token in the function env. Use an SSM **SecureString** (or Secrets Manager) read at runtime, or an API Gateway API key / JWT authorizer Power Automate can send. Prefer Azure AD on the HTTP action. If you keep a static token: high entropy, rotation, and store it only in the Power Automate secret store â€” not in Lambda config.  
**Verification:** Confirm `VALID_TOKEN` is not visible on `GetFunctionConfiguration`. Missing/wrong `Authorization` must 401/403 and must not `Scan`.

---

**Severity:** Medium  
**Confidence:** Confirmed  
**Category:** Testing  
**Location:** `tests/dealership-api/` (no new tests in the PR)  
**Finding:** No negative tests for missing header, wrong Bearer, empty `VALID_TOKEN`, or `GET /dealerships` skipping `verifyBodyHash`.  
**Impact:** A broken or bypassed check can ship unnoticed.  
**Recommendation:** Add handler tests: no auth â†’ 401; bad token â†’ 403; matching token â†’ Scan; POST still requires signed-request/body hash.  
**Verification:** Those cases fail on current `main` and pass on the PR branch.

---

**Severity:** Low  
**Confidence:** Likely  
**Category:** Reliability  
**Location:** `verifyAuthorization.mjs` `tokensMatch`  
**Finding:** Length is compared as JS string length, then `timingSafeEqual` uses UTF-8 buffers. A mismatched buffer length throws **before** the handler `try/catch` and becomes a 500.  
**Impact:** A crafted `Authorization` header can error the route instead of 403.  
**Recommendation:** Compare `Buffer` lengths (or hash both sides, then `timingSafeEqual`).  
**Verification:** Non-ASCII Bearer of the same JS length as `VALID_TOKEN` returns 403, not 500.

---

**Decision: Request changes**

**Blocking findings:**  
High â€” shared Bearer in Lambda env in front of a full PII `Scan`, with `Authorizer: NONE` and CORS `*`.

**High-priority findings:**  
Medium â€” no auth negative tests.

**Other recommendations:**  
Fail-closed when `VALID_TOKEN` is unset (already 403). Do not log `Authorization`. Confirm SSM `/dealership/apiauthorizer/validtoken` exists as SecureString before deploy. Keep POST/DELETE on the signed authorizer.

**Testing gaps:**  
Unauthenticated GET, invalid Bearer, happy-path GET, and POST still rejected without signed headers.

**Infrastructure risks:**  
`Authorizer: NONE` lets anyone invoke Lambda (cost/DoS) up to burst 200. Table SSE is off (`SSEEnabled: false`) â€” pre-existing, worse if the list endpoint is easier to call.

This is an acceptable **integration** approach for Power Automate only if the token is treated as a production secret. As written, it is not equivalent to the signed-request authorizer and is not safe to merge without tightening secret handling and tests.

Hire / booking agreement generation in **my-sandbox** (`zhenwei.shen@carbiz.com.au.uat`) is two processes, not one. The live **PDF** path is **Nintex DocGen**. The live **signable form** path is **FormTitan**. The names overlap, which is why this looks like a single DocGen feature.

Source of truth: metadata retrieved from my-sandbox on 14 Sep 2026.

## What actually produces the PDF

After Stripe pre-auth succeeds, `Booking_Automation_3` (active, after-save on `Booking__c`) publishes `DocGen_Request__e`. That event is the only unmanaged publisher found for hire/booking RA PDFs.

```
Booking__c after save
  â†’ Booking_Automation_3
    â†’ create DocGen_Request__e
      â†’ DocGenRequestTrigger
        â†’ DocGenRequestHandler
          â†’ Central_DocGen_Dispatcher
            â†’ Loop.RunDocGenAsync (Nintex)
              â†’ PDF attached / emailed by delivery option
```

`DocGenRequestHandler` requires `Source_Record_Id__c`, `Ddp_Id__c`, `Delivery_Option_Id__c`, and `Correlation_Id__c`, all as Salesforce IDs. It then starts `Central_DocGen_Dispatcher`, which only calls Nintex `Run DocGen Package` with `recordId`, `ddpId`, and `deliveryOptionId`.

`Ddp_Id__c` is documented on the event as the **Nintex DocGen package (`Loop__DDP__c`) Id**.

## Booking Automation 3 â€” when the RA PDF is requested

The flow runs on create/update of `Booking__c`, except when `Order_Products_Created__c`, `Customer_Owner_Relationship__c`, or `Vehicle__c` just changed.

The RA branches sit under **Booking Fees Added or Removed**:

| Condition | Correlation | What the flow intends |
|---|---|---|
| `Stripe_PreAuth_Message__c = Success`, fees changed, no DingGo | `BOOKING_RA_STANDARD` | Generate RA, attach to booking, **do not email the customer** |
| Pre-auth success, DingGo present, status just became `In Progress`, hire exists, billing = Full Chargeback | `BOOKING_RA_DINGGO_FULL_CHARGEBACK` | DingGo RA attach-only |
| Same DingGo hire start, other billing | `BOOKING_RA_DINGGO` | DingGo RA (default of that decision) |

A separate event, `BOOKING_PREAUTH_ATA`, generates an ATA document against the **Accident**, not the booking.

The email templates in the same flow say the rental agreement â€œwill be sent across shortlyâ€ and is â€œfor your records onlyâ€. That matches the attach-only delivery options, not the FormTitan sign-now link.

## Nintex packages in my-sandbox

These `Loop__DDP__c` records exist on `Booking__c`:

| Package | Delivery options in sandbox |
|---|---|
| Carbiz RA Generate PDF Only | New Booking fees added |
| Carbiz RA Sent to customer Docgen | Send Email, Wrong RA Sent |
| DingGo RA Docgen Send to customer | Send Email |
| DingGo RA Docgen Send Only to DingGo | Send Email |
| Min Test Carbiz RA Generate PDF Only | Min Test Carbiz |

`Booking_Automation_3` does **not** use those sandbox IDs. It hardcodes production-style IDs (`a1U9s000â€¦`). Those IDs are not `Loop__DDP__c` records in my-sandbox. The handler still accepts them because they look like Salesforce IDs; Nintex then has no package to run. That is a sandbox data/config gap, not a missing dispatcher.

The flow also leaves `Document_Route__c` and `Source_Application__c` blank. Correlation text (`BOOKING_RA_STANDARD`, etc.) is the only route label.

## FormTitan is the other â€œagreementâ€ path

This path builds a **URL**, not a Nintex PDF.

1. Formula field `Booking_Agreement_DocGen_Link__c` (name is leftover):

```
https://carbiz.formtitan.com/ft1ab6c3391655960313689?fld3=<Booking Id>
```

2. Active autolaunched flow `Generate_booking_agreement_link` (v2) builds a longer FormTitan URL (`ft153e08141660229111958_copy`) by loading:
   - Booking â†’ Accident â†’ Customer Account
   - Vehicle
   - In/out `Vehicle_Inspection__c` (kms, fuel)
   - Damage-assessment `ContentVersion`
   - Up to 10 `Booking_Fee__c` lines  
   then outputs `formTitanLink`.

3. Screen flows that wrap that subflow are **inactive/draft**:
   - `Booking_Screen_Flow_Generate_Booking_Agreement` (Draft)
   - `Booking_Screen_Flow_Booking_Agreement_DocGen_Link` (Draft) â€” older hardcoded FormTitan link

So the vault line â€œ`Generate_booking_agreement_link` produces the signable agreementâ€ is correct for **FormTitan**. It is not the Nintex PDF path.

Manufacturer packs (Kia / JAC / Mahindra / Direct Hire Rental Agreement) are separate Nintex DDPs on `Form_Submission__c`. `Form_Submission_V3` does not publish `DocGen_Request__e`.

## How this generalises to other documents

The reusable pattern is:

1. A business flow decides **which package** and **which delivery option**.
2. It publishes `DocGen_Request__e` with record Id, DDP Id, delivery-option Id, and a correlation Id.
3. `DocGenRequestHandler` validates and starts `Central_DocGen_Dispatcher`.
4. Nintex renders the PDF and delivers it (attach, email, etc.).

Hire / booking agreement is that pattern with three RA packages plus one ATA package, triggered after successful Stripe pre-auth â€” not by the FormTitan â€œGenerate Booking Agreementâ€ link.

Source of truth: my-sandbox (`zhenwei.shen@carbiz.com.au.uat`).

## What `DocGen_Request__e` contains

It is a **High Volume** platform event, **Publish After Commit**. After commit, Salesforce delivers it to `DocGenRequestTrigger`. The event itself is not a queryable business record.

**Platform fields (always present):** `ReplayId`, `EventUuid`, `CreatedDate`, `CreatedById`.

**Custom fields in the org:**

| Field | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Source_Record_Id__c` | Yes | Salesforce Id Nintex runs against (Booking Id for an RA; Accident Id for ATA) |
| `Ddp_Id__c` | Yes | `Loop__DDP__c` Id â€” which DocGen **package** to run |
| `Delivery_Option_Id__c` | Yes | `Loop__DDP_Integration_Option__c` Id â€” attach only, email, etc. |
| `Correlation_Id__c` | Yes | Trace / intended idempotency key. Hire RA uses values like `BOOKING_RA_STANDARD:<BookingId>` |
| `Document_Route__c` | No | Audit label (e.g. `BOOKING_PREAUTH_ATA`). Hire RA publishers leave this blank |
| `Source_Application__c` | No | Which app requested it. Hire RA publishers leave this blank |
| `Requested_By_User_Id__c` | No | Audit only. Hire RA publishers leave this blank |

`Booking_Automation_3` only sets the four required fields. Example for the standard hire RA:

- `Source_Record_Id__c` = the Booking Id  
- `Ddp_Id__c` = hardcoded `a1U9s0000007mDvEAI`  
- `Delivery_Option_Id__c` = hardcoded `a1S9s0000005UKBEA2`  
- `Correlation_Id__c` = formula intended as `BOOKING_RA_STANDARD:<Booking Id>`

**Not on the event:** customer name, fees, vehicle, Word tags, PDF bytes, output file Id, success/fail, or a pointer to the template. Nintex reads that from the source record after the run starts.

`DocGenRequestHandler` only checks that the four required fields are populated and that the three Id fields (plus `Requested_By_User_Id__c` if present) parse as Salesforce Ids. It does **not** check that the DDP or delivery option exists in this org.

## How the event is processed

```
Booking save (after commit)
  â†’ Booking_Automation_3 creates DocGen_Request__e
    â†’ DocGenRequestTrigger (after insert)
      â†’ DocGenRequestHandler.handle()
        â†’ Central_DocGen_Dispatcher (autolaunched Flow)
          â†’ Loop.RunDocGenAsync(recordId, ddpId, deliveryOptionId)
            â†’ Nintex merge + deliver
```

1. After the booking transaction commits, the platform event is published.
2. `DocGenRequestTrigger` runs as **Platform Integration User** (System Administrator), via `PlatformEventSubscriberConfig` `DocGenRequestTrigger_Config`, **batch size 1**.
3. Invalid events are skipped. The only signal is a `WARN` debug line with route, source record Id, and correlation Id. Nothing is written back to the Booking.
4. Valid events start `Central_DocGen_Dispatcher` with those seven inputs. In my-sandbox that Flow does **one** thing: call Nintex `Loop__RunDocGenAsync`. It does not route to S-Docs or FormTitan (the vault still describes a three-vendor fan-out; this orgâ€™s dispatcher does not).
5. The dispatcher passes only `recordId`, `ddpId`, and `deliveryOptionId` into Nintex. `correlationId`, `documentRoute`, `sourceApplication`, and `requestedByUserId` are Flow inputs and are **not** sent to `RunDocGenAsync`.
6. `RunDocGenAsync` is asynchronous. The Flow stores the invocable output automatically and then ends. Nothing reads that output. The publisherâ€™s Flow has already continued.

Nintex then:

- loads `Loop__DDP__c` and the Word file on `Loop__DDP_File__c`
- queries the Booking plus related objects configured on the package (Vehicle, Accident, Account, Booking fees, Job, Form Submission, additional drivers, and some unrelated User/Contact/Account rows)
- merges tags in the `.docx`
- converts to PDF (`Loop__Output__c` = PDF on the RA delivery options)
- delivers according to the delivery option (attach to the Booking, and/or email)

## Where the template is saved

The template is **not** in the event and **not** in AWS. It lives in Salesforce as Nintex config plus a classic Document.

```
Loop__DDP__c                    package (Ddp_Id__c)
  â””â”€ Loop__DDP_File__c          which Word file, order, type=docx
       â””â”€ Loop__Document_ID__c  classic Document Id (015â€¦)
            â””â”€ Folder "DocGen Files"
  â””â”€ Loop__DDP_Integration_Option__c   delivery option (Delivery_Option_Id__c)
  â””â”€ Loop__Related_Object__c           what to query for merge fields
```

Hire RA examples in my-sandbox:

| Package | Word Document in folder `DocGen Files` | Output file name pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Carbiz RA Generate PDF Only | `Carbiz - Vehicle Rental Agreement  - 10.08.2026` | `Updated Booking fees Rental Agreement` |
| Carbiz RA Sent to customer Docgen | same title, separate Document Id | `Rental Agreement <<Accident_Accident_Number>>` |
| DingGo RA (customer / DingGo-only) | `Carbiz - Vehicle Rental Agreement  - 25.03 Final - Copy` | `Rental Agreement for <<Booking_Name>>` |

The `.docx` itself is the template: Nintex tags such as `<<Accident_Accident_Number>>` and `<<Booking_Name>>` are inside that Word file. Package records also point at related objects so those tags can be filled.

Delivery options for those RA packages attach as **Attachment** and output **PDF**. Option names encode the behaviour: `New Booking fees added` (store on record), `Send Email`, `Wrong RA Sent`.

All of those RA `Loop__DDP__c` rows are **`IsActive = false`** in my-sandbox. Combined with `Booking_Automation_3` still pointing at production-shaped Ids (`a1U9s000â€¦`) that are not packages here, a hire RA event can be accepted by the handler and still fail inside Nintex.

## How the caller knows it was generated â€” and where to find it

The caller **does not get a callback**. There is no `DocGen_Complete` event, no Booking field updated by the dispatcher, and `Correlation_Id__c` is not written onto the Nintex job. Publishing the event only means â€œrequest accepted after commit.â€

To see whether a PDF exists, look **on the source record** and in **Nintexâ€™s job object**.

**1. On the Booking (or Accident for ATA)**  
Related Files / Notes & Attachments. RA delivery options use `Attach_As = Attachment`. Nintexâ€™s own job link formula uses the classic download URL `/servlet/servlet.FileDownload?file=<id>`, so the stored file is a classic Attachment/Document Id, not a custom â€œDocGen resultâ€ field. Expected names follow the package pattern above (`Updated Booking fees Rental Agreement`, `Rental Agreement <accident number>`, etc.).

**2. Nintex job row: `Loop__Document_Request__c`**  
Filter `Loop__Object_Id__c` = the Booking Id.

| Field | Use |
|---|---|
| `Loop__Status__c` | `Pending`, `Complete`, `Emailed`, `Merged`, `Looped`, `Error` |
| `Loop__Document_Id__c` / `Loop__Document_Name__c` | generated file |
| `Loop__Error_Id__c` / `Loop__Error_Message__c` | failure |
| `Loop__LOOP__c` | which package ran |
| `Loop__Email_Link__c` | if it was emailed |

That is the only structured â€œdid it work?â€ record in the org. Nothing in unmanaged Apex or `Booking_Automation_3` reads it.

**3. If the delivery option emails**  
The PDF also goes to the recipient configured on that Nintex option. The Booking still usually gets an attachment copy (`Attach_As = Attachment`). There is no Carbiz status field that says â€œemail sent.â€

**4. Debug only**  
Skipped requests: Apex debug from `DocGenRequestHandler`. Failed Nintex runs: `Loop__Document_Request__c` with `Error`, plus Nintex/Apex exception email if the invocable throws. The hire Flow does not wait and does not branch on those outcomes.

So for hire / booking agreement: `Booking_Automation_3` publishes and moves on (for example to `Update_Customer_Vehicle`). A user or a later process finds the PDF on the Bookingâ€™s attachments, or an admin finds the job under `Loop__Document_Request__c`. The correlation Id is useful in logs, not as a join key to the file.

## Documentation Update Suggestions

- **Existing notes to update:** `20-products/Carbiz-Salesforce/07-events-and-integrations/platform-events/Platform Event Catalogue.md` and `13-architecture/Architecture Decisions.md` (AD-13) â€” they still say the dispatcher fans out to S-Docs, Nintex, and FormTitan. In my-sandbox it only calls `Loop.RunDocGenAsync`.
- **New note to create:** `20-products/Carbiz-Salesforce/07-events-and-integrations/outbound/DocGen Request Processing.md`
- **Suggested folder:** `20-products/Carbiz-Salesforce/07-events-and-integrations/outbound/`
- **Suggested backlinks:** Platform Event Catalogue, Integration Failures, Booking to Hire, AD-13
- **Reason:** callers need a documented completion model (there isnâ€™t one) and a documented file location (`Loop__Document_Request__c` + attachments on the source record, templates in folder `DocGen Files`).

[PR #435](https://github.com/CarbizRentals/carbiz-aws-iac/pull/435) (`update-scp` â†’ `main`) updates **AWS Organizations Service Control Policies** in the management-account Control Tower guardrail files. There is **no application or Lambda code** in this PR.

Author: Rajiv. One commit: `update SCP policies`. Empty PR body.

**Where it applies**

| OU / account set | Files |
|---|---|
| Nonprod (`nonprod-ou-carbiz_dev`) | 4 `aws-guardrails-*.json` |
| Production | `aws-guardrails-XxjgAw.json` |
| Security | `aws-guardrails-lHSUin.json` |

These are org-level **Deny** guardrails. They cap every IAM principal in attached accounts, including admins.

---

**What actually changed**

Most of the +1237/âˆ’1157 is **JSON re-indent** (4 spaces â†’ 2) and **moving statements between SCP files**. Control Tower does that to stay under the 5 KB SCP size limit. Those moves do not change the combined policy if every SID still exists on the OU.

The real policy change is **Bedrock region residency**:

1. **New statement `GRBEDROCKAURESIDENCY`** on nonprod (`uoJuby`) and production (`XxjgAw`):

```json
"Action": ["bedrock:InvokeModel*"],
"Effect": "Deny",
"Condition": {
  "StringNotEquals": {
    "aws:RequestedRegion": [
      "ap-southeast-2",
      "ap-southeast-4",
      "us-east-1"
    ]
  }
}
```

2. **`bedrock:InvokeModel*`** is added to the `CTMULTISERVICEPV1` region-deny **NotAction** list so the generic â€œno APIs outside allowed regionsâ€ rule does not fight the new Sid. Invoke is then limited by `GRBEDROCKAURESIDENCY`.

3. **`GRREGIONDENY` still exempts `bedrock:*`** on some files (e.g. `BYyrjt`). That means Bedrock *management* APIs can still be called outside AU; **inference** (`InvokeModel*`) cannot.

Security OU file is indent-only.

---

**Impact**

**Intended:** Stop Bedrock **model invocation** outside **Sydney, Melbourne, and N. Virginia**. That is an AU data-residency / sovereignty control for prompts and completions. `us-east-1` stays allowed (common for some Bedrock models and global endpoints).

**Who feels it**

- Dev/UAT and **prod** accounts under those OUs.
- Any app, notebook, or console user calling Bedrock in `us-west-2`, `eu-west-1`, etc. will get **implicit deny**, even with a valid IAM allow.
- `InvokeModel`, `InvokeModelWithResponseStream`, and similar `InvokeModel*` actions.

**What does not change**

- Creating/listing Bedrock resources in other regions may still work where `bedrock:*` is exempt from `GRREGIONDENY`.
- Non-Bedrock region rules stay as they were at OU level (stricter 2-region `CTMULTISERVICEPV1` plus a 4-region `GRREGIONDENY` still both attach in nonprod).
- Merging the PR **does not** change AWS by itself. Impact starts when this SCP product is **deployed to the management account** and Organizations updates the live policies.

**Risks to watch**

- Workloads already invoking Bedrock in a non-AU region will break after deploy.
- Confirm Melbourne (`ap-southeast-4`) is enough for the models you use; not every model is in every region.
- Statement reshuffle: `GRCONFIGAGGREGATIONAUTHORIZATIONPOLICY` left `uoJuby` but is still in `BYyrjt`, so it should still apply on nonprod. Worth a SID checklist after deploy so nothing was dropped.

**Bottom line:** The PR is for **org SCP refresh**, mainly to **pin Bedrock inference to AU (plus `us-east-1`)**. Operational impact is on Bedrock callers only, and only after the management-account SCP deployâ€”not on merge.

I put the keep/swap/move map and the three integration shapes in [AWS DocGen replacement considerations](C:\Users\Zhenwei Shen\.cursor\projects\c-Users-Zhenwei-Shen-Documents-Workspace-carbiz-aws-iac\canvases\aws-docgen-replacement-considerations.canvas.tsx) so you can open it beside the chat. A canvas is a live view next to the transcript; I used it because this is a cross-system design checklist, not a single answer.

## Recommended seam

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph keep["Do not touch"]
    Pubs["Publisher Flows\nBooking_Automation_3\nForm_Submission_V3\ninvoice flows"]
    PE["DocGen_Request__e"]
    H["DocGenRequestHandler"]
  end

  subgraph swap["Only Salesforce change"]
    D["Central_DocGen_Dispatcher\nNamed Credential callout"]
  end

  subgraph aws["New AWS service"]
    API["Accept request"]
    Q["Async render"]
    R["Pull SF data + merge"]
    W["Attach PDF / email"]
  end

  Pubs --> PE --> H --> D --> API --> Q --> R --> W
```

Publishers already send four fields: source record, package Id, delivery-option Id, correlation Id. AWS should treat those as the public contract. Do not make each Flow call AWS.

## Areas that matter

**1. Salesforce compatibility (this is the â€œminimum impactâ€ test)**  
Keep publisher Flows, the event, the trigger, and the handler. Change one invocable in the dispatcher. If a design needs new fields on `Booking__c`, new wait steps, or edits to every RA branch, it has already failed the impact goal.

**2. Opaque Id catalogue**  
Flows hardcode Nintex Ids (`a1U9s000â€¦` in my-sandbox, which do not match sandbox packages). AWS must accept those same strings (or a stable alias you introduce once in the dispatcher) and map them to template + delivery. Do not ask Salesforce to start sending template names unless you are willing to edit every publisher.

**3. Who reads Salesforce data**  
The event has no customer, vehicle, or fee payload. Nintex queries Booking plus related objects (Accident, Account, Vehicle, fees, Job, additional drivers). AWS must do the same with a least-privilege integration user. Decide Composite vs several queries, field-level security, and that this user can read RA data and write files â€” and nothing else.

**4. File write-back**  
Staff find the RA on the Booking. AWS must create a Salesforce File or Attachment on `Source_Record_Id__c` with the current filename pattern (`Updated Booking fees Rental Agreement`, `Rental Agreement <accident number>`). If the file is only in S3, Salesforce users and later automations break.

**5. Email is part of DocGen, not an extra**  
Delivery options include attach-only, email customer, email DingGo, and â€œwrong RA sent.â€ Choose SES (AWS owns mail) or Salesforce email (keeps deliverability and email logs in the org). Either way, the Booking still needs the attached PDF.

**6. Async, not a synchronous API**  
`RunDocGenAsync` returns before the PDF exists. A requestâ€“response API Gateway call will hit Salesforce callout and Lambda timeouts once Word merge + PDF + file upload run. Accept `202` quickly, render on SQS/Step Functions, then write back. The dispatcher must stay fire-and-forget unless you deliberately add a completion event.

**7. Two trust boundaries**  
- Salesforce â†’ AWS: Named Credential, private API, no public â€œgenerate any recordâ€ endpoint.  
- AWS â†’ Salesforce: Connected app / JWT, integration user, scoped connected app policies.  
Do not trust a client-supplied user Id or role. `Requested_By_User_Id__c` is audit only.

**8. Idempotency**  
`Correlation_Id__c` is the only key today, and it is **not** passed to Nintex. AWS should dedupe on it (`BOOKING_RA_STANDARD:<BookingId>`). Platform events can replay. Without this, fee updates will attach duplicate RAs.

**9. Completion and failure (today this is a gap)**  
There is no callback. Min impact means Flows still do not wait. AWS still needs a status store (DynamoDB plus optional write to a Salesforce log, or a later `DocGen_Result__e`). Operators need to find Error the way they use `Loop__Document_Request__c` now. Do not log merge payloads.

**10. Template fidelity and legal content**  
The RA is a Word file in folder `DocGen Files` with `<<tags>>`. You must inventory every tag and related-object row, then prove pixel/legal equivalence. A new HTML template that â€œlooks closeâ€ is a business-risk change, not a like-for-like replace. Version templates in S3/git; do not leave them only in the org.

**11. Scope is larger than hire RA**  
Same dispatcher is used for DingGo RA, ATA on Accident, manufacturer RAs on `Form_Submission__c`, and invoice DocGen. Design the AWS service as a **document runner** (record + package + delivery), and migrate one package first. FormTitan `Generate_booking_agreement_link` is out of scope.

**12. PII, retention, and environment split**  
RA data includes customer, licence, and accident details. Keep it in the Salesforce account / encrypted S3, short-lived working objects, no CloudWatch payload dumps. Separate staging and production credentials. Salesforce already mixes hardcoded prod Ids in a sandbox â€” the AWS catalogue must be environment-specific.

**13. Quotas, cost, and operability**  
Each RA is several Salesforce API calls plus PDF render. Bound concurrency, add a DLQ, alarm on age-in-queue and attach failures. Salesforce daily API limits are shared with Xero, OpsIQ, and portals. Prefer CDK, matching the rest of the middle tier.

**14. Cutover**  
Dual-run one package Id through AWS while others stay on Nintex. Sandbox is already broken for hardcoded Ids, so UAT must use a mapping table, not a copy of prod Ids. Rollback is â€œdispatcher calls Nintex again.â€

## Three approaches

| Approach | Salesforce change | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| **Dispatcher swap** (recommended) | One Flow action + Named Credential | Minimum impact, keeps AD-13 |
| Relay `DocGen_Request__e` to EventBridge | Channel membership, new consumer, still keep publishers | If you want zero callout from the dispatcher |
| Each Flow calls AWS | Edits every publisher | Avoid |

Relay is viable only if you accept Event Relay work. `DocGen_Request__e` is **not** on `AWS_Event_RelayChannel` today. A callout from the dispatcher is a smaller Salesforce change than teaching the existing relay a new event.

## What I would not do in v1

- Make Booking Flows wait for the PDF  
- Push the full merge payload from Salesforce (duplicates the data model and increases PII on the wire)  
- Replace FormTitan e-sign in the same service  
- Require new Booking fields for â€œdocument readyâ€

`Booking_Automation_3` does **not** check whether the PDF landed on the Booking (or Accident). There is **no timeout**, because it never waits.

## What the flow actually does

It is an after-save Flow on `Booking__c` with **no scheduled paths** and **no Wait/Pause**. After it creates `DocGen_Request__e`, the next element is always `Update_Customer_Vehicle` â€” not a file lookup.

Standard hire RA:

```
Booking Fees Added or Removed
  â†’ create DocGen_Request__e  (BOOKING_RA_STANDARD)
    â†’ Update Customer Vehicle?
```

DingGo RA (including Full Chargeback):

```
â€¦ â†’ create DocGen_Request__e
  â†’ Update Customer Vehicle?
```

ATA:

```
Generate ATA attached to Accident Event
  â†’ Booking Fees Added or Removed   (may then publish an RA event)
```

The Flow never queries `Attachment`, `ContentDocumentLink`, `ContentDocument`, or `Loop__Document_Request__c`. A successful **create event** is the only â€œsuccessâ€ it cares about. Nintex runs later, asynchronously, after that transaction has already committed.

`Central_DocGen_Dispatcher` is the same shape: it calls `Loop.RunDocGenAsync`, stores the invocable output, and ends. Nothing reads that output, and nothing reports back to Booking Automation.

## The ATA lookup is not a generation check

`Check_if_ATA_already_completed_beforehand` looks for an existing `Form_Submission__c` on the Accident with a specific ATA record type. If `AtaID` is null, it publishes a **new** ATA DocGen event; if one already exists, it skips.

That is â€œdo we already have an ATA form submission?â€, not â€œdid Nintex finish writing this PDF?â€ and not a poll with a timeout.

## Timeout

There is **no configured wait or timeout** on this path.

- No Flow Wait for a time interval
- No scheduled path like â€œcheck Files in 2 minutesâ€
- No retry loop
- No â€œif no attachment by T, fail / re-publishâ€

If generation is slow or fails, Booking Automation has already moved on. The booking save does not sit open waiting for the PDF.

The only clocks that still apply are Salesforce/Nintex platform limits (Flow CPU, event delivery, Nintexâ€™s own async job), not a Carbiz-defined â€œdocument readyâ€ timeout. Those are not wired back into this Flow.

So: the caller does not learn that the document exists. A person (or a later process) has to look at Notes & Attachments on the Booking/Accident, or at `Loop__Document_Request__c` for that record Id.

my-sandbox inventory: **Nintex DocGen 20.22.1**, **23 packages**, **31 delivery options**, **12 of which email**. A compact view is in [Nintex replacement areas](C:\Users\Zhenwei Shen\.cursor\projects\c-Users-Zhenwei-Shen-Documents-Workspace-carbiz-aws-iac\canvases\aws-docgen-replacement-considerations.canvas.tsx).

## 1. Central dispatcher

**Now:** `DocGen_Request__e` â†’ `DocGenRequestHandler` â†’ `Central_DocGen_Dispatcher` â†’ `Loop.RunDocGenAsync`. That invocable is a managed Loop action.

**Recommended:** Keep the event, trigger, and handler. Change only the dispatcher to an async Named Credential callout to AWS. Delete the Loop action. Uninstall is impossible while this Flow still references `Loop__RunDocGenAsync`.

## 2. Publisher Flows (business triggers)

**Now:** `Booking_Automation_3`, `Form_Submission_V3`, invoice DocGen flows, and others publish `DocGen_Request__e` with hardcoded `Ddp_Id__c` / `Delivery_Option_Id__c` (often production-shaped Ids). They do not wait for the PDF.

**Recommended:** Leave publishers in place. Do not teach each Flow to call AWS. After cutover they keep sending the same four fields; AWS maps them. That is the minimum Salesforce behaviour change.

## 3. Package and delivery catalogue

**Now:** The catalogue is `Loop__DDP__c` + `Loop__DDP_Integration_Option__c`. Packages cover Booking RA, DingGo RA, ATA, manufacturer RAs (`Form_Submission__c`), invoices (`Order`), SOC (`Litigation__c`), PayBiz, Direct Hire. Delivery names encode attach-only vs email (`New Booking fees added`, `Send Email`, `Store Only on Record`, `Send Invoice to DingGo`).

**Recommended:** Move this to **custom metadata or an AWS catalogue** with a stable key (`BOOKING_RA_STANDARD`, `DINGGO_RA_CUSTOMER`, â€¦) plus: template version, attach yes/no, email yes/no, From, To expression, filename pattern. Keep accepting todayâ€™s Salesforce Ids during dual-run, then stop storing Loop Ids in Flows.

## 4. Flows that query Loop objects

**Now:** `Form_Submission_V3` does `Get DocGen Package` on `Loop__DDP__c` where `Loop__Description__c` = `{ProviderId}-RA`. That is a live unmanaged dependency. Uninstall will fail until it is rewritten.

**Recommended:** Replace that lookup with custom metadata (provider â†’ document key) **before** uninstall. Same for any report, list view, or Flow that reads `Loop__*` objects.

## 5. Word templates

**Now:** `Loop__DDP_File__c.Loop__Document_ID__c` points at classic **Document** records in folder **DocGen Files** (`.docx` with `<<merge tags>>`). Related objects on the package tell Nintex what to query (Booking â†’ Accident, Vehicle, Account, fees, Job, additional drivers).

**Recommended:** Export every `.docx` and related-object map before uninstall. Store versioned templates in S3/git. Recreate the merge graph in AWS. Classic Documents can stay in the folder after uninstall; Loop file rows cannot.

## 6. PDF render

**Now:** Nintex merges tags, converts to PDF (`Loop__Output__c` = PDF), runs as **Platform Integration User**.

**Recommended:** AWS (Lambda + a Word/PDF engine) does merge and convert. Salesforce no longer needs Loop licenses for render. Prove legal equivalence on hire RA first, then invoices and ATA.

## 7. Attach the file to the Salesforce record

**Now:** Delivery options use `Attach_As = Attachment`. Staff find the PDF on the Booking / Accident / Order / Form Submission. `Loop__Document_Request__c` links the file via classic `/servlet/servlet.FileDownload`.

**Recommended:** AWS writes a **Salesforce File** (ContentVersion + ContentDocumentLink) on `Source_Record_Id__c`, using the current filename patterns. Do not leave the only copy in S3. Prefer Files over classic Attachment so you are not recreating a deprecated store.

## 8. Email (this is what uninstall also removes)

**Now:** Nintex **Salesforce Email** delivery, not a Carbiz Apex mailer. Typical pattern:

| Piece | Current behaviour |
|---|---|
| Transport | Salesforce email servers, via Nintex |
| From | Org-wide addresses (`on-hire@`, `assessments@`, `warranty@`, `kiarentals@`, `noreply@`, and similar) |
| To | Merge tag `<<Form_Submission_Email>>`, or a hardcoded partner/staff mailbox (DingGo help desk, AEI assessor, â€¦) |
| Body | Not in `Loop__Message__c` (null in sandbox). Template is selected in the Nintex UI |
| Attachment | The generated PDF |
| Activity | Salesforce email / activity on the record, if Nintex logs it that way |

Hire RA examples: attach-only does **not** email; `Carbiz RA Sent to customer` emails the form-submission address from `on-hire@`; DingGo-only emails the DingGo mailbox from `assessments@`.

**Recommended:** Split â€œgenerateâ€ from â€œsendâ€:

1. AWS attaches the PDF to the record.
2. **Salesforce sends the email** with that File attached (Apex `SingleEmailMessage` or the existing **SendBetterEmail** package), using the same org-wide From and the To/CC rules from the new catalogue.

That replaces Nintex email without standing up SES as a customer-mail channel, and it keeps From-address, bounce handling, and activity in the org. Put To/From/template in custom metadata so uninstall does not delete the rules.

Do **not** rely on Loop email templates after uninstall â€” they are package data.

SES is only worth it if you want AWS to own deliverability end-to-end; then you must write `EmailMessage` (or equivalent) back to Salesforce or ops lose the activity timeline.

## 9. Job status and support

**Now:** `Loop__Document_Request__c` statuses: Pending, Complete, Emailed, Merged, Looped, Error. Nothing in unmanaged code reads it. Uninstall **deletes** these rows.

**Recommended:** Export recent jobs before uninstall. Add a small `DocGen_Job__c` (or AWS DynamoDB + a Salesforce status field) with correlation Id, source record, package key, status, error, ContentDocument Id. Still no need for publishers to wait.

## 10. Identity, licences, permission sets

**Now:** Subscriber runs as Platform Integration User. Packaged permission sets: `DDP_Administrator`, `DDP_User_All`, deprecated `DDP_Admin` / `DDP_User`, `Nintex_DocGen`, `Automation_Forms`, unmanaged `Docgen_Integration_User`. Loop licenses are managed on the installed package.

**Recommended:** Named Credential + connected app for AWS. A least-privilege integration user that can read the merge graph and create Files/emails â€” not a copy of DocGen Admin. Unassign Loop licenses and packaged permission sets **after** dual-run, **before** uninstall.

## 11. UI, buttons, Lightning app

**Now:** Vault lists a **Loop** Lightning app. Nintex ships VF pages (`loop__ddpEdit`, `loop__selectemailtemplate`), buttons, and â€œgenerateâ€ entry points on records. Staff may still generate packages manually.

**Recommended:** Inventory page layouts, Lightning pages, and custom buttons for Loop components. Replace manual generate with a Salesforce action that publishes `DocGen_Request__e` (same path as automation). Remove Loop tabs from apps. Uninstall fails if a layout still hosts a Loop button.

## 12. Other DocGen vendors (do not uninstall those)

**Now:** Same org also has **S-Docs**, **FormTitan**, and **Concord / Opero Documents**. FormTitan still owns the signable hire-agreement **URL** (`Generate_booking_agreement_link`). That is not Nintex.

**Recommended:** Scope uninstall to **Nintex DocGen only**. Do not fold FormTitan e-sign into the AWS PDF service. Confirm S-Docs/Concord are not silently covering documents you thought were Loop.

## 13. Historic files vs historic Loop records

**Now:** Generated PDFs sit on business records; templates sit in DocGen Files; queue rows sit on `Loop__Document_Request__c`.

**Recommended:** PDFs on Bookings/Orders **stay** (they are Salesforce Files/Attachments, not Loop records). Export templates. Accept that Loop queue/history is lost unless exported. Do not bulk-delete attachments as part of uninstall.

## 14. Package uninstall itself

**Now:** Salesforce will refuse uninstall while any of these remain: Flow actions/queries on `Loop__*`, Apex references, Lightning/VF, reports, permission-set groups including packaged sets, packaged email templates in use.

**Recommended order:**

1. Dual-run AWS behind the dispatcher; Nintex still installed.
2. Point all packages at AWS; Loop actions unused.
3. Rewrite `Form_Submission_V3` (and any other Loop SOQL).
4. Export templates, delivery rules, recent job rows.
5. Remove Loop UI and permission-set assignments.
6. Uninstall **Nintex DocGen 20.22.1** in sandbox first, then production.
7. Rollback while dual-run exists: dispatcher calls Loop again. After uninstall, rollback is restore package + data, which is slow â€” do not uninstall until AWS is proven.

## 15. Reliability, PII, environments

**Now:** Fire-and-forget; failures are Nintex errors and debug logs. Merge data is customer, licence, and accident PII. Sandbox packages are inactive and Ids do not match what Flows hardcode.

**Recommended:** Async queue, idempotency on `Correlation_Id__c`, DLQ, alarms. Do not log merge payloads. Environment-specific catalogues (do not copy prod Loop Ids). Same org-wide From addresses in staging only if they are safe test mailboxes.

---

**Minimum-impact target:** Salesforce still publishes `DocGen_Request__e`. AWS renders and attaches. Salesforce sends the email with that File. Then Loop is unused and can be uninstalled.

## Documentation Update Suggestions

- **Existing notes to update:** `20-products/Carbiz-Salesforce/07-events-and-integrations/outbound/Index.md` and `99-archive/Index.md` (DDP permission sets) â€” add uninstall blockers and that email is Nintex Salesforce Email, not SendBetterEmail.
- **New note to create:** `20-products/Carbiz-Salesforce/13-architecture/Nintex DocGen Replacement.md`
- **Suggested folder:** `20-products/Carbiz-Salesforce/13-architecture/`
- **Suggested backlinks:** AD-13, Platform Event Catalogue, Business Capabilities (document generation), Lightning Applications
- **Reason:** uninstall and email are separate workstreams from PDF render; the org still queries `Loop__DDP__c` in `Form_Submission_V3`.

If this split is acceptable, next decision is whether customer/partner email should stay in Salesforce after attach (recommended) or move to SES.

Nintex today bundles three things into one package: the `.docx`, the related-object/SOQL map, and the delivery option. The runner (`Loop.RunDocGenAsync`) reads all three from Loop objects. An independent **package service** should own those three and expose only a resolved snapshot. The **runner** should only render, attach, and (if you keep it there) send mail.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph callers["Callers â€” unchanged"]
    SF["Salesforce\nDocGen_Request__e\npackage key + record Id"]
  end

  subgraph pkg["Package service â€” config only"]
    Cat["Catalogue"]
    Tpl["Templates"]
    Map["Data mapping"]
    Del["Delivery options"]
    Cat --> Tpl
    Cat --> Map
    Cat --> Del
  end

  subgraph run["Runner â€” execution only"]
    R["Resolve package\nPull SF data\nMerge PDF\nAttach / email"]
  end

  SF -->|"key, recordId, correlationId"| R
  R -->|"GET package by key"| pkg
```

The contract the runner should depend on is a **versioned snapshot**, not Loop Ids:

- `key` â€” `BOOKING_RA_STANDARD` (plus alias table for old `a1Uâ€¦` Ids during dual-run)
- `version` â€” immutable once published
- `templateUri` â€” S3/git object
- `mapping` â€” which objects/fields/relationships fill which tags
- `delivery` â€” attach, email, From, To expression, filename

Salesforce does not send the template or the mapping. The runner does not embed them.

## Options

### 1. GitOps catalogue (repo + S3)

Templates and mapping live as versioned files in git (`packages/booking-ra-standard/v12/template.docx`, `mapping.json`, `delivery.json`). CI publishes to an env-specific S3 prefix. The runner reads `key + version` from S3. No admin API.

| Fits | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| Legal templates that change rarely and need review | Salesforce admins lose the Nintex â€œedit package in the orgâ€ UX |
| Strongest audit: PR, env promotion, rollback = redeploy previous version | A mapping typo needs a deploy, not a checkbox |
| No extra runtime service | Alias map for old DDP Ids still needs a small file or Dynamo table |

**Use when** package changes should follow the same path as code.

### 2. Dedicated AWS package service (API + DynamoDB + S3)

A small service owns CRUD and publish:

- S3: binary templates
- DynamoDB: package metadata, mapping JSON, delivery options, aliases, `activeVersion`
- API: `GetPackage(key)`, `List`, `Publish` (admin only)

The DocGen runner is a **client**. Admins (later) get an internal UI or CLI. Salesforce still only sends a key.

| Fits | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| True decoupling: swap the PDF engine without touching config | You must build auth, audit, activate/deactivate, and who can publish |
| Runtime activate of a new version without redeploying the runner | More moving parts than GitOps |
| Same API can serve hire RA, invoices, ATA later | Mapping stored as JSON can become an unreviewed production edit |

**Use when** ops need to turn a delivery option on/off without a release, or several runners will share one catalogue.

### 3. Salesforce-owned catalogue (custom objects or custom metadata)

Replace `Loop__DDP__c` / `Loop__DDP_File__c` / `Loop__Related_Object__c` / `Loop__DDP_Integration_Option__c` with unmanaged Carbiz objects (or CMDT). AWS queries Salesforce at run time, or a sync job copies them to S3.

| Fits | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| Closest to todayâ€™s admin mental model | **Not independent** â€” catalogue still lives in the org you are trying to thin |
| Custom metadata is deployable and environment-safe | Custom objects are editable in prod with no PR |
| Helps uninstall Loop without inventing a new UI | Runner stays coupled to Salesforce schema; CMDT cannot store `.docx` |

**Use as a transition** (alias table + delivery flags in CMDT) or if a Salesforce admin must remain the only editor. Do not make this the long-term source of templates and mapping if the goal is a decoupled AWS service.

### 4. Hybrid (recommended)

Split by **how often it changes and who should approve it**:

| Concern | Owner | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Stable key + old Loop Id aliases | Custom metadata **or** Dynamo alias table | Flows keep sending Ids; service translates |
| Template `.docx` + mapping JSON | Git â†’ S3 (Package service read-only) | Legal content, reviewable, versioned |
| Delivery (attach vs email, From, To expression) | Package service (Dynamo), published from git | Changes more often than the Word file; still not in the runner |
| Execute | Runner only | Fetches snapshot, pulls record data, writes File |

Salesforce never stores the Word file after Loop is gone. The runner never contains `if (dinggo) email help@â€¦`. The package service never queries customer records.

That is the same separation Nintex had internally (package vs run), moved off the managed package.

## What not to do

- Hard-code mapping or email rules inside the render Lambda â€” that recouples every new document type.
- Copy Nintex `Loop__SOQL__c` as free-form SOQL in the catalogue â€” that is an injection and over-privilege risk. Mapping should be an **allowlisted graph** (object, relationship, fields, filters), compiled to queries by the runner.
- Let Salesforce send the full mapping on `DocGen_Request__e` â€” duplicates the data model and puts PII-adjacent config on the event.
- Give the package service write access to Bookings â€” config and execution stay on opposite sides of the trust boundary.

## How this meets â€œminimum Salesforce impactâ€

Publishers still send `Ddp_Id__c` / `Delivery_Option_Id__c`. The **package service** resolves those to a key and snapshot. After dual-run you change the dispatcher (or CMDT) to send the stable key. Uninstall Loop only after no Flow queries `Loop__DDP__c` (`Form_Submission_V3` is the known one).

## Comparison

| | GitOps only | AWS package service | Salesforce catalogue | Hybrid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Decoupled from runner | Yes | Yes | Partial | Yes |
| Decoupled from Salesforce | Yes | Yes | No | Almost (aliases may stay in CMDT) |
| Admin UX | PRs | API / later UI | Native SF | PR for template; small UI later for activate |
| Env isolation | Branch/prefix | Table per env | CMDT per org | Both |
| Rollback | Redeploy version | Point `activeVersion` back | Deploy old CMDT | Point version back |
| Build cost | Lowest | Medium | Medium in SF | Medium, staged |

**Recommendation:** treat the package service as a real module (option 2â€™s API), with **git as the write path** (option 1) so templates and mapping cannot be silently edited in production. That is option 4. Salesforce keeps only the request key.

- **Existing notes to update:** the Notion [DocGen Replacement Solution](https://app.notion.com/p/3dce109ba14e806cacafc8dfb5a9c170) table row â€œPackage and delivery catalogueâ€ â€” it currently says â€œcustom metadata or AWS catalogueâ€ as one cell; these are different options.

- **Suggested folder:** `20-products/Carbiz-Salesforce/13-architecture/`
- **Suggested backlinks:** AD-13, outbound Index, DocGen Replacement Notion page
- **Reason:** the catalogue vs runner split is the main decoupling decision after the dispatcher seam.

text:
Reviewing the three proposed data mapping options for the AWS package service. Preparing additional alternatives and design recommendations.

Security risks such as SOQL injection, PII exposure, and over-fetching are the primary concerns. Salesforce should remain the source of truth with minimal impact. The focus is on architecture analysis rather than implementation.

Composite API is already used in this codebase. SOQL lists in DynamoDB would avoid new Apex but introduce injection risk, difficult schema validation, and strict request limits. Apex endpoints stored in DynamoDB are being evaluated next.

Apex endpoints stored in DynamoDB keep mapping logic inside Salesforce. This avoids SOQL injection risks but introduces endpoint confusion and extra Apex maintenance. AWS would still need to call back into Salesforce for write-back.

The third approach has Salesforce gather the full payload before sending it to AWS. This makes AWS a pure renderer with no Salesforce queries. Mapping stays entirely within Salesforce.

The payload-gathering approach increases Salesforce impact. Large PII payloads risk Lambda and API limits. Event sizes and duplicate data on the wire are concerns. Salesforce callout timeouts and dispatcher conflicts are possible. Payload schema versioning becomes a nightmare. Retrying renders without re-fetching from Salesforce is difficult.

A better alternative is an allowlisted object graph. Define root objects, relationships, fields, and filters in declarative JSON. An AWS query builder compiles this into Composite or SOQL. This keeps mapping logic inside Salesforce while avoiding large payloads and excessive Salesforce calls.

A single Apex provider invoked by package key is a cleaner alternative. AWS would store only the package identifier. Salesforce would switch on that key to return a structured DTO. This replaces multiple endpoints with one service and keeps mapping logic inside Salesforce. It reduces DynamoDB endpoint confusion but requires new Apex code.

GraphQL or Composite Graph could also work. That path may be overkill.

The allowlisted object graph is safer than raw SOQL. It remains structured and versioned with the package. Integration user privileges still govern field-level security.

A hybrid model is emerging. A declarative graph would cover most packages. Named Apex expanders would handle exceptions like additional drivers or unrelated users.

A cached snapshot or platform event carrying only record IDs is another path. AWS would then use Composite retrieve against known field lists defined in the package mapping.

Change Data Capture or AWS replicas are too complex and violate the minimum impact goal. Salesforce Reports are also not recommended.

Raw SOQL in DynamoDB and arbitrary endpoint URLs in DynamoDB should both be rejected. Raw SOQL carries injection risk. Arbitrary endpoints create SSRF and confused deputy vulnerabilities.

Rejecting fat payloads from every publisher Flow. This breaks the minimum Salesforce impact goal and exposes PII, size limits, and retry complexity.

The preferred design is a declarative allowlisted mapping in DynamoDB or S3. AWS compiles this into Composite queries. The delivery record stores the template reference alongside the mapping.

For packages needing custom SOQL, AWS should call one fixed Salesforce REST endpoint. DynamoDB stores only the package key and a data mode flag. A single Apex class handles the request via a strategy switch. This eliminates arbitrary URLs from DynamoDB.

A fully centralized Apex aggregator is the simplest alternative. AWS would stay lightweight, but mapping changes would require Apex deployments instead of DynamoDB updates.

Option 3 can be refined further. Dispatcher Apex gathering data before calling AWS preserves existing publisher Flows. This keeps mapping logic outside the package service.

Field-level allowlists and Composite Graph are worth considering. The integration user must still follow least privilege principles.

Concrete security constraints are taking shape. No SOQL string should ever reach AWS from DynamoDB without an allowlist compiler. Payloads must not be logged. If the payload-gathering approach is chosen, encryption is required. AWS must reject arbitrary SOQL from callers entirely.

The recommendation will be grounded in the existing loan-cars composite API usage. The final question will ask whether mapping changes should trigger an Apex deployment or a catalogue publish.
